story.conflict: A bride must judge both the father who accepted payment to disappear and the groom who treated choosing her family as something he could purchase.
story.hook: A groom paid the bride's father to break his promise to walk her down the aisle. The father took the cash and pretended to be ill.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF THE CHOICE WAS HERS
story.premise: A groom pays the bride's father to break his promise to walk her down the aisle, and the father accepts the money and pretends to be ill.
story.punchline: She left the soup in the kitchen and made the next call herself.
story.script: Alice drove over with soup after her father said he was too ill for the wedding. His new shoes were back in their box. He admitted he wasn't ill. He told her Tom had offered three thousand dollars if he stayed away. Alice asked whether he'd taken it. He said he was behind on rent. She put down the soup. Her father said he'd felt ashamed, and Tom had called the arrangement easier for everybody. Alice asked which part had been easier for her. He had no answer. She called Tom from the kitchen. He said her father could have refused. Accepting the money proved he wasn't someone she should depend on. Alice asked why that decision had been made without her. Tom said he'd been protecting her from disappointment. She said he'd paid to create the disappointment he now wanted credit for predicting. Her father offered to send the money back. Tom said that wouldn't change what he'd done. Alice said it wouldn't change what either of them had done. Her father asked whether he could still walk her down the aisle after returning it. Alice looked at the shoes she'd helped him choose. She said she hadn't decided what happened next, and neither man would decide for her. Then she told Tom the wedding was on hold. She left the soup in the kitchen and made the next call herself.
story.twist: The groom uses the father's acceptance of the bribe as proof that paying him to stay away was justified.

youtube.description: A bride learns that her groom paid her father to miss the wedding, and that her father accepted the deal.
youtube.title: The Shoes He Was Paid Not to Wear

story.conflict: A sister must insist that paying for her brother's work does not mean giving him the appliance he agreed to repair.
story.hook: Her brother tried to sell her own washing machine back to her. He'd collected it for a repair, then claimed it wasn't worth fixing.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SHE HAD ALREADY PAID
story.premise: A brother tries to sell his sister her own washing machine after taking it and an eighty-dollar payment to repair it.
story.punchline: The blue star was still there.
story.script: Rosa went to his shop because he'd told her she needed a replacement. Ben pointed to a refurbished washer and offered a family price: four hundred dollars. Rosa lifted the lid. A little blue star was drawn beneath it. Her daughter drew it when they moved house. Rosa asked whether this was her machine. Ben said he'd managed to get it running after all. She reminded him she'd already paid eighty dollars when he collected it. He said that had been for looking at it. Rosa said he'd quoted eighty for the repair. Ben told her she'd agreed to replace it, so he assumed she didn't want the old one. She asked when an assumption had become permission to sell it. He said he'd put work into it. She said she'd paid for that work. He called their mother and put her on speaker. Their mother said Ben's shop was struggling and Rosa shouldn't expect family to do everything for nothing. Rosa told her about the eighty dollars. Then she asked Ben what else he'd repaired before deciding it belonged to him. He stopped talking about the discount. Rosa said she wanted her washer delivered home, as they'd originally agreed. Ben said he'd bring it after closing. That night, Rosa loaded the laundry and lifted the lid once more. The blue star was still there. Nobody had needed to sell her a replacement for it.
story.twist: The machine he called uneconomical to repair is the refurbished model he now offers her at a supposed family discount.

youtube.description: A sister recognizes her own washing machine in her brother's shop after paying him to repair it and being told it was beyond saving.
youtube.title: The Blue Star in His Refurbished Stock

story.conflict: A worker must find a way forward when the person expected to describe her work honestly uses references to keep her dependent on his business.
story.hook: Her old boss publicly called her a thief, then offered to rehire her for less. He'd been using that lie to block her job applications.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SHE DESERVED AN HONEST REFERENCE
story.premise: A former boss publicly repeats a false theft allegation he has used to block a worker's applications, then offers to rehire her for less.
story.punchline: Her next application didn't carry his number.
story.script: Nora went back to the shop after two interviewers asked about missing cash. Her old boss, Gary, said it loudly enough for the staff to hear: other employers weren't keen on taking a thief. Nora asked which money he meant. He said references were a private business matter. She asked why he was announcing it at the counter, then. Gary lowered his voice and said her old chair was still there. The wage would be twenty percent less. Nora asked whether he wanted somebody he'd described as dishonest handling his money again. He said he knew how to manage her. Her former team leader, Sal, came over. Nora asked Sal whether cash had ever been missing while she worked there. Sal said no. Gary told her to get back to the stockroom. Nora asked whether he'd invented the allegation because she'd left. He said people needed to learn that walking out had consequences. She'd worked her notice and trained her replacement. Gary pointed toward the empty chair and said she could stop making things difficult. Nora didn't sit down. She asked Sal whether she'd describe the work they'd actually done together to another employer. Sal said yes. Nora still didn't have another job. She had somebody willing to tell the truth, and she wasn't accepting a lower wage to make Gary's lie go away. Her next application didn't carry his number.
story.twist: The employer who says she cannot be trusted is prepared to employ her again once his lies have weakened her bargaining position.

youtube.description: A worker learns her former boss has poisoned her references, then hears his cheaper offer to take her back.
youtube.title: The Empty Chair at Twenty Percent Less

story.conflict: A man must respond to his girlfriend's financial need without letting either woman decide which relationship he should return to.
story.hook: His girlfriend admitted taking money from his ex-wife to sabotage their dates. She'd been offered rent money to make him regret leaving the marriage.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF HIS CHOICE WASNT FOR SALE
story.premise: A man's girlfriend admits accepting rent money from his ex-wife to sabotage their dates and make him regret the divorce.
story.punchline: For once, the evening was going ahead exactly as he'd chosen.
story.script: Daniel had booked the same restaurant three times. Each time, Chloe canceled or started an argument before they reached the door. Then his ex-wife, Lisa, called and mentioned a detail he'd only told Chloe. He asked Chloe how Lisa knew. She said they'd been talking. Then she told him about the payments. Lisa had offered help with overdue rent if Chloe made the relationship feel like a mistake. Daniel asked whether their first date had been paid for too. Chloe said no. That had been real. The money came later, when she'd been afraid of losing her flat. Daniel said he could understand being afraid. He couldn't turn that into permission to sell their private life to somebody else. Chloe said she'd wanted to stop. He asked why he'd needed to find out before that happened. She didn't answer. Daniel called Lisa and asked what she'd expected. She said he'd needed reminding that the divorce hadn't solved everything. He said she'd paid to create a problem and called it a reminder. Lisa asked whether this meant he was coming home. He said no. Chloe offered to return the money. Daniel said she could do that without asking him to decide their future that evening. After she left, he called the restaurant. They still had his reservation. He changed it to one person. For once, the evening was going ahead exactly as he'd chosen.
story.twist: The girlfriend originally dated him sincerely, but accepted payments afterward to create the unhappiness his ex-wife hoped would bring him back.

youtube.description: A man discovers that his ex-wife has been paying his girlfriend to make their relationship fail.
youtube.title: The Dinner She Was Paid to Cancel
